label: rem:lp-sdp-bootstrap-prior-art
title: Prior art for symmetry-reduced bootstrap programs and machine-checked dual certificates
html:
The dual-certification procedure in Solver-external rationalized dual-slack optimality and uniqueness certification draws upon four established mathematical and computational traditions, while assembling them to solve a distinct finite-dimensional algebraic selection problem.

Conformal, sphere-packing, and interior-point bootstraps

The pairing of primal operator weights against dual exclusion functionals enters modern high-energy physics with Riccardo Rattazzi, Vyacheslav S. Rychkov, Erik Tonni, and Alessandro Vichi [rattazzi-rychkov-tonni-vichi2008], who reformulated crossing symmetry and unitarity in four-dimensional conformal field theory as a linear feasibility problem. Sheer El-Showk, Miguel F. Paulos, David Poland, Slava Rychkov, David Simmons-Duffin, and Alessandro Vichi [elshowk2012] subsequently introduced the extremal-functional method, reading the physical spectrum from the zeros of the optimal dual slack vector c - A^{\mathsf{T}} u^* along the boundary of the allowed region. Because polynomial conformal blocks become severely ill-conditioned at binary double precision, David Simmons-Duffin [simmons-duffin2015] developed native arbitrary-precision primal--dual interior-point semidefinite solvers, while Paul J. Goulart and Yuwen Chen [goulart-chen2024] formulated the homogeneous self-dual interior-point conic architecture underlying Clarabel. In discrete geometry, Henry Cohn and Noam Elkies [cohn-elkies2003] and Maryna S. Viazovska [viazovska2017] demonstrated that a dual auxiliary functional whose slack vanishes only on the shell radii of a single configuration pins an algebraic object uniquely---establishing optimality and uniqueness of the E_8 lattice packing by strict complementary slackness.

Symmetry-reduced block decomposition

Reducing a noncommutative positivity cone to scalar and low-rank inequalities indexed by irreducible representations originates with Philippe Delsarte [delsarte1973], who diagonalized commutative association schemes into linear programs over spherical and Krawtchouk characters. Alexander Schrijver [schrijver2005] and Dion Gijswijt, Alexander Schrijver, and Hajime Tanaka [gijswijt-schrijver-tanaka2006] extended character diagonalization to noncommutative centralizer *-algebras via the Terwilliger algebra, and Karin Gatermann and Pablo A. Parrilo [gatermann-parrilo2004] established the general Peter--Weyl and Young-diagram isotypic block reduction for group-invariant semidefinite and sum-of-squares programs. Whenever an observable lies in the center of H_n(q), orthogonality of central idempotents collapses matrix semidefinite positivity \sum_\lambda y_\lambda \mathrm{tr}(M_\lambda^{\mathsf{T}} M_\lambda) \ge 0 to the scalar partition inequalities y_\lambda \ge 0 on every nonempty Wedderburn block.

Nuclear reduced-density-matrix and trace-loop positivity

In quantum many-body physics, direct variational minimization over the two-body reduced density matrix subject to (D, Q, G) particle--hole positivity was brought into angular-momentum and isospin-coupled (J, T) nuclear structure calculations by Brecht Verstichel, Helen van Aggelen, Dimitri Van Neck, Paul W. Ayers, and Patrick Bultinck [verstichel-vanaggelen2009]. In noncommutative operator algebras and gauge theory, Miguel Navascués, Stefano Pironio, and Antonio Acín [navascues-pironio-acin2007] introduced the trace Gram matrix hierarchy \tau(b_i^* b_j) \succeq 0 over word monoids, and Vladimir Kazakov and Zechuan Zheng [kazakov-zheng2022, kazakov-zheng2023] combined Makeenko--Migdal loop equations with trace Gram positivity to bound matrix models and lattice Yang--Mills plaquette expectations.

Certified rational dual witnesses in proof assistants

The algebraic principle that a single dual multiplier vector certifies a global primal bound goes back to Gyula Farkas [farkas1902] and to the resolving multipliers (shadow prices) of Leonid Vitaliyevich Kantorovich [kantorovich1939]. Separating untrusted numerical optimization from formal kernel verification was pioneered at scale in the Flyspeck proof of the Kepler conjecture by Thomas C. Hales and collaborators [hales2017], where external linear programs generated dual certificates verified inside HOL Light. In the Coq ecosystem, Sylvie Boldo, Catherine Lelay, and Guillaume Melquiond [boldo-lelay-melquiond2015], Pierre Roux [roux2016], and Assia Mahboubi and Thomas Sibut-Pinote [mahboubi-sibut-pinote2021] developed rigorous real-analytic, interval, and Cholesky-positivity certificates for untrusted numerical and semidefinite oracles, while Martin Dvořák and Vladimir Kolmogorov [dvorak-kolmogorov2024] formalized linear-programming duality and Farkas lemmas over linearly ordered fields in dependent type theory.

Distinctive synthesis in this paper

Unlike continuum conformal or infinite-volume lattice bootstraps---which bound truncated slices of an infinite-dimensional correlator hierarchy---this paper formulates arbitrary-precision conic programs directly on finite-dimensional Hecke and Temperley--Lieb normal-form strata at the fixed modulus q_0. Once an interior-point solver identifies a candidate primal--dual pair, rationalizing the dual multiplier vector u^* reduces primal optimality and strict complementary-slackness support uniqueness to exact identities over an arbitrary linearly ordered ring, placing the numerical solver entirely outside the trusted kernel.
